definitions.definition: (engineering, physics) The ratio of useful work to energy expended. Often given the symbol η.
The extent to which time is well used for the intended task.

quote.citation: 1951 October, H. A. Vallance, “Across Denmark by Lyntog”, in Railway Magazine, page 658:
quote.text: Even at the busiest periods, an air of quiet orderliness pervades the hall, and the first impression gained by the traveller is one of efficiency, neatness and cleanliness.

quote.citation: 2012 September 7, Phil McNulty, “Moldova 0-5 England”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: The display and result must be placed in the context that was it was against a side that looked every bit their Fifa world ranking of 141 - but England completed the job with efficiency to record their biggest away win in 19 years.

definitions.definition: The extent to which a resource is used for the intended purpose.
(dated) The quality of producing an effect or effects.

quote.citation: 1594–1597, Richard Hooker, edited by J[ohn] S[penser], Of the Lawes of Ecclesiastical Politie, […], London:  […]  Will[iam] Stansby [for Matthew Lownes], published 1611, →OCLC, (please specify the page):
quote.text: The manner of this divine efficiency being far above us.
